title: Snowshoeing at Grouse Mountain (North Vancouver)
description:
Join us for a winter outing to the peak of Grouse Mountain for a scenic snowshoeing experience. After a panoramic Skyride gondola trip to the top, we will explore the mountain on snowshoes. Have lunch (not included in the fee) at the chalet.
This trip is recommended for people comfortable walking up to 4 kilometers in the snow. Participants must dress for cold mountain weather.
Snowshoe rental and gondola ticket are included in the fee. Please note the last day for refund is December 29th, 2026.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.

title: Line Dance: Beginner 1
description:
Learn line dance in this beginner class. This is a good place to start for new dancers. This is where you learn many of the basic 'rhythm calls' required for line dancing. This is the place to be if you want to become a comfortable line dancer. Dancing takes practice, time and patience. It's one step at a time- while having fun!Learn about musicality, balance, co-ordination, memory and styling techniques. Get started dancing today and meet friendly people sharing the same interest in dance!
Please wear comfortable, smooth sole shoes to allow for easy dance movements.
There is a possibility that a dancer will be moved to an alternate session if it is deemed that they are not registered in the correct level. No transfers will occur after the third class.
Refund Policy: Reminder- refunds are available if cancelled at least 7 days before the start of the activity. Once the activity starts, refunds are prorated by the number of days remaining and a refund fee of 10% on the original price will be applied. NO REFUNDS after the third class in a registered activity.

title: Natural Dyeing: Creating Natural Dye Baths
description:
Discover how colour can be created from plant materials through an introduction to natural dyeing. Participants will learn the basic process of preparing natural dye materials and creating and working with natural dye baths.
The workshop will feature an indigo vat alongside additional natural dye colours, allowing participants to experiment with resist techniques inspired by shibori, dipping and overdyeing. Through layering colours and patterns, participants will create a unique naturally dyed textile piece while learning about the processes behind natural colour.
*Participants under the age of 13 must be accompanied by a parent/guardian.

title: Natural Dye: Painting on Fabric
description:
Explore natural colour through a hands-on textile painting workshop. Participants will learn how dyes and pigments derived from natural materials can be transformed into paints and applied directly to fabric.
Creating and using natural dye pastes, participants will experiment with colour, pattern and layering before creating their own naturally dyed textile piece to take home. The workshop introduces natural dyes in an approachable and creative way while exploring the relationship between plants, colour and textiles.
*Participants under the age of 13 must be accompanied by a parent/guardian

title: Intro to Digital Photography: DSLR & Mirrorless
description:
Ready to take your photography to the next level? This hands-on course introduces the essential camera settings and techniques needed to gain greater creative control over your images. Learn how aperture, shutter speed, and ISO work together to control exposure, while exploring focus, depth of field, and composition. Designed for photographers who own a DSLR or mirrorless camera and want to move beyond automatic mode, this course will help you build technical confidence and develop your photographic skills.

title: Art Explorations: Collage Edition
description:
Collage is so much more than cutting and pasting, as we did as kids. Artists like Picasso and Matisse embraced collage as a way to bring together materials and ideas to create fresh, exciting art forms. From flat panels to booklets, decorative cards to personal journals, collage offers endless ways to express yourself. Break the rules of composition and experiment with personal mementos, old artwork, found papers, fabrics, and more. Explore landscapes, still life, portraits, and abstract designs as you discover the limitless possibilities of contemporary collage!
Instructor: Christy Dunsmore

title: 55+ Lifestyle Lecture: Managing Glaucoma
description: Learn about glaucoma and approaches to managing eye health. This presentation will provide information, practical tips, and resources to support those living with or affected by glaucoma.

title: 55+ Lifestyle Lecture: Tax Planning for Long-Term Care
description:
Navigating the health care and senior benefits system can be challenging. Many seniors and their caregivers are not prepared when the situation arises, and they are suddenly faced with the research, requirements, paperwork, and often difficult decisions around choosing the best option for their changing needs. Awareness and proper planning can ease the transitions between the varying levels of care. From aging at home to long-term care, join us for an informative workshop on the health care options available for you or your loved ones. Topics will include: levels of care in retirement, potential care costs, income planning to reduce taxes and care costs, and working with Health Authorities.
Instructor: David Perkins, CFP®, EPC, CEA

title: 55+ Lifestyle Lecture: Healthy Hearing
description: Join Network Hearing Health for a presentation on Healthy Hearing. Learn about different degrees of hearing loss and practical strategies for managing hearing health in everyday life.

title: Busy Bees: Adult Participation
description: You and your little one keep busy with many activities in this fun and creative playtime. Painting and pasting, musical activities, stories, songs and a variety of play stations are all designed to spark your child’s imagination. title: Line to Design Series
description:
Line to DesignWe are providing a space to explore your creative side. Come join a series of art and design sessions to get those creative juices going and thinking outside the 'box'. Participants are given an image for inspiration and a template to trace. Templates will be based on ornaments, book jackets, gift tags, bookmarks, t-shirts and different shapes like pyramids, cubes, etc. There will be different types of shapes, so you can see how your illustrations will 'flow' from side to side and top to bottom. From there, you will be encouraged to create artwork.
A light box will be available for tracing. You can use pen and ink, watercolours, watercolour pencils, etc. Please bring your own supplies. No supplies are provided.
* Please bring a 9 X 12 watercolour sketchbook and your favourite colouring medium to the sessions.
No design experience necessary. Come and have fun. This activity is offered in partnership with the Confederation Seniors Association.
There will be a volunteer onsite assisting during the session but this series is an opportunity to explore your creativity independently.

title: Watercolour Wonders
description:
Join us for a fun-filled adventure in our Watercolor Wonders class designed especially for creative kids aged 6-7! In this exciting class, young artists will explore the magical world of watercolor painting. Through playful activities, they'll learn basic techniques like blending, lifting, and layering colors while experimenting with different brushes and papers.
Each week, we'll focus on a new theme, from vibrant landscapes to whimsical creatures, allowing children to express their imagination and build confidence in their artistic skills. With plenty of encouragement and guidance, every child will create their very own masterpiece to take home!Get ready to splash some color, make new friends, and discover the joy of painting in a fun, supportive environment! All materials are provided. Just bring your creativity and a big smile!
Instructor: Tami Murray

title: Drawing & Painting: Portraiture & Still Life
description:
Unleash your artistic potential in our engaging Drawing & Painting: Portraiture and Still Life class! This course is perfect for budding artists looking to refine their skills while exploring two fundamental aspects of art.
In the portraiture segment, students will learn techniques for capturing likeness and expression, using a variety of mediums. Through guided exercises and individual projects, participants will develop their understanding of proportions, shading, and the unique features that make each person special.
The still life portion of the course focuses on composition, color theory, and the interplay of light and shadow. Students will arrange their own still life setups, experimenting with different materials and styles to create striking, personal works of art.
Join us for an inspiring journey into the world of portrait and still life art, and leave with your own stunning creations! All materials are included.
Instructor: Tami Murray

title: Blacksmithing Level 1: Basic
description:
This introduction to blacksmithing starts with learning the importance of safety in a blacksmith's shop. The hands-on component has students lighting a coal forge, as well as making a coat hook and dinner triangle. Students will learn how to heat mild steel in a forge and shape it with a hammer and anvil. Steel-toed boots recommended.
This Level 1 workshop is considered an introductory blacksmithing course. Successful completion of the course fulfills the prerequisite for taking BVM's Level 2 courses.
Cancellations within 48 hours of the start of the course will not be issued a refund.

title: Blacksmithing Level 2: Cupid's Arrow & Heart
description:
Touch the heart of a special someone with a hand-forged “cupid’s arrow.” We’ll learn the easy way to make arrow-points and add heart-shaped fletching to the opposite end and give it a twist so that it flies straight to its target. We’ll use simple but clever designs and a chisel to split the steel to create the sides of the heart. When the arrow is complete, it will need a hand-shaped heart, hot-shaped using only a vice and tongs.
This Level 2 workshop is considered an intermediate blacksmithing course. Successful completion of the course fulfills the prerequisite for taking BVM's Level 3 courses.
Online registration is not available for this course. To register please call 604-297-4565.
Cancellations within 48 hours of the start of the course will not be issued a refund.

title: Urban Safari Rescue Society & Lunch at The Roadhouse Grille
description: Calling all animal lovers! Join us for an exciting, guided tour of the Urban Safari Rescue Society in Surrey and meet over 350 fascinating animals, including rescued exotic species, reptiles, and more! Explore the amazing world of insects in the Bug Lab and learn about animal conservation and why exotic pets sometimes need a new home. After our safari adventure, we'll enjoy lunch (not included in the fee) at The Roadhouse Grille, a local family-owned restaurant serving homemade food prepared with fresh ingredients. Step back in time and enjoy it's nostalgic retro atmosphere, complete with classic decor for an old-fashioned roadside-diner feel. Come along for a day filled with fascinating animals, learning, great food, and plenty of fun! This trip is fully accessible. Please note the last day of refund is January 26.

title: Flute or Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Georgia Tuhten
description:
Students can sign up for private flute, beginning piano or theory lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: Georgia Tuhten.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

description:
Expand your skills and learn the basics of screen printing. At its core, screen printing is an extension of drawing, so if you have interest in mark making, abstract, life drawing and anything in between, you can translate your themes through the screen printing process. Step by step process will be explained on how to do emulsion based screen printing as well as how incorporate it into your every day practice.
Instructor: Janine Schroedter
$20 materials fee applicable. Additional supplies required. See STUDENT SUPPLY LIST in Notes section below.

title: Martial Gym for Functional Fitness
description: Rather than memorizing sequences of exercises, exercisers are taught simple goals/guidelines to create their own exercise routine that is relevant and effective. Classes are tailored specifically to seniors, to protect as well as have fun. The goal is to empower seniors through improved flexibility, balance, co-ordination, strength and knowledge. With new movement patterns for fitness and a new understanding of how to effectively neutralize hazards, seniors are better equipped to maintain their quality of life for longer. Frequent interaction and feedback are used to improve quality of movement and understanding. Martial Gym taps into gymnastics for fun and variety and ancient Chinese secrets for health and effectiveness. Drawing on aspects of both martial arts and rhythmic gymnastics, learn to stimulate your body and mind's adaptability to different situations. Using light objects, games, music and interaction with other participants, progress beyond mirroring an instructor's movements to improving your own balance, strength, coordination and self-defence skills. Participants must be able to get down onto a mat on the floor and back up again, in order to participate in this class.

description:

Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Reserve in Advance: Weight Room Orientation
description:
“Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.”

The goal of the weight room orientation is to provide someone new to exercise or new to the facility a basic introduction to the weight room.

  • A 45 minute safety weight room orientation. Participants will receive training on: safe practices in the weight room, proper use of equipment and a review of policies and etiquette.
  • We will provide you with the basics of how to use weight and cardio equipment. You will learn how to start, stop and change settings on cardio machines, change seat height and weight selections on machines, and have a discussion of proper form on the weight machines.
  • All instructors are experienced and certified.
  • NOTE: an orientation is NOT a personal training session.
  • Schedules are subject to change.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha / Core
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered with an emphasis on the core muscles.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Reserve in Advance: Figure Skating
description:
Practice the sport of Figure Skating at this drop-in. Participants must wear figure skates and confidently skate at Star 2+ (backwards cross over, 3-turns, toeloop, back spin). Skaters must have their own skates. (Recreational skates are not appropriate).
Reserved spots will be forfeited 10 minutes after the program has started. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist. Participants must have their own equipment.
Coaching is not permitted.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Play to Learn Preschool
description: Play to Learn is all about learning through play in a fun, welcoming environment. Children explore a variety of exciting activity stations including art, music, science exploration, group games, and daily routines designed to spark curiosity and creativity. Through hands-on experiences and guided play, children build confidence, friendships, independence, and important physical, social, and learning skills. Children must be required age within one month of the program start date, ready to attend on their own and be able to use the toilet independently. Dress comfortably and bring a small, nut-free nutritious snack.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Flow
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This energetic class improves strength, flexibility and balance with a continual flow of postures. Through this practice you cleanse the body, stimulate the cardiovascular system, develop your agility and balance and build muscle tone. Some classes may have extra emphasis on core strength. This class is for able-bodied and experienced students.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha / Core
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered with an emphasis on the core muscles.

title: Drawing & Cartooning
description:
Bring your imagination to life! Students develop their drawing skills as they create expressive characters, dream up exciting stories, and turn their ideas into their own comic books and cartoon strips. Along the way, they explore a variety of traditional drawing techniques, including the vibrant styles of manga and anime.
Instructor: Chris Lupien.

title: Animation & Character Design
description:
What makes a cartoon character funny, fierce, or totally unforgettable? In this activity, children explore cartoon styles and characters from their favourite media to discover what makes a character truly stand out. Through playful experimentation with shapes, structure, and all kinds of body types, they learn how to bring their characters to life with personality and flair. From quirky shapes to unexpected designs, young artists will think outside the box, push their creativity, and dream up unique characters all their own!
Instructor: Chris Lupien.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This energetic class improves strength, flexibility and balance with a continual flow of postures. Through this practice you cleanse the body, stimulate the cardiovascular system, develop your agility and balance and build muscle tone. Some classes may have extra emphasis on core strength. This class is for able-bodied and experienced students.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.00.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Bronze Medallion
description: Prerequisites: Must be 13 years old OR have Bronze Star. Understand the lifesaving principles embodied in the four components of water rescue education: judgment, knowledge, skill and fitness. Rescuers learn self rescue techniques, defence and release methods, and tows and carries in preparation for challenging rescues involving conscious and unconscious victims of various types, including spinal injuries and circulatory emergencies. Lifesavers develop stroke efficiency and endurance in a timed swim. Includes the CPR-A certification. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.

title: Bronze Cross
description: Prerequisite: Bronze Medallion. Designed for lifesavers who want the challenge of more advanced training, including an introduction to safety supervision in aquatic facilities. Swimmers develop proficiency at performing patient assessments, managing aquatic spinal injuries and preventing loss of life in a variety of aquatic emergencies, while developing stroke endurance and fitness training skills. Includes the CPR-C certification and is one of the prerequisite awards for all advanced Lifeguarding and Leadership training programs. It is also worth two Grade 11 high school credits. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.

title: Sports & Games: Soccer
description: Introduce your child to the joy of soccer! This program combines fun, interactive games and fundamentals of soccer designed specifically for preschoolers. Led by experienced preschool instructors, children will explore the basics of the game—like dribbling, kicking, and scoring goals—using age-appropriate equipment to build confidence and coordination. Through these engaging activities, children will also practice listening skills and learn to follow simple, multi-step instructions. Children must be required age within one month of the program start date, ready to attend on their own and be able to use the toilet independently. Dress comfortably in shoes and clothes that your child can easily move around in. Bring a water bottle with your child’s name on it.

title: Intro to Gliders
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Gliders skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Animation Design: Building Worlds & Characters
description:
Students will work in Photoshop and Sketchbook Pro to develop animation designs, with characters being the focus. Background and prop designs will also be covered, and students will be encouraged to focus on their strengths. Sketching on paper will be encouraged in the early stages of design exploration to move quickly through a set of ideas. Emphasis will be placed on the differences between designing for 2D vs 3D animation and we'll learn the importance of strong silhouettes, functional design and specific personality in the characters the students will be creating. Instructor: Eris Fitz-James.

ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 6
description: Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 5. These swimmers will become proficient at deep water skills including stride entries and compact jumps. They’ll develop lifesaving kicks such as eggbeater and scissor kick. Breaststroke, front crawl, and back crawl are further developed. ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Singing Mamas
description: Join a warm, welcoming, safe space where mothers come together for the therapeutic benefits of singing and music. Its more than just music, singing is clinically proven to boost mood, release happy hormones, and support postpartum well-being. This unique class is designed to nurture connection, relaxation and bonding with your baby (max age 24 months) and other moms, caregivers, grandmas who are going through similar changes and stages of life with no judgment. It truly takes a village. <u>Absolutely NO</u> prior singing experience necessary. Come sing, connect, and embrace the journey of motherhood with us! ** No Class Feb 15Brought to you by Shadbolt in your Community Instructor: Bryony Ollier – Certified “Singing Mamas” Leader

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Acro Dance: Introduction
description:
This class combines acrobatics & dance and is a pre-requisite to taking Acro Dance I. Children learn the basics of tumbling, back flexibility/strength, balances and choreography to music. The fees in the Sunday Acro classes are more expensive than other days of the week as they have an assistant.
Instructor: Sydney Poland
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs,

title: Acro Dance 1/2: Short-Term
description:
This class combines acrobatics & dance and is a pre-requisite to taking Acro Dance 2 and/or 3. Children learn variations of the tumbling skills learnt in Acro Dance - Introduction and/or Acro Dance 1 as well as basic contortion, balance variations and choreography to music. These are put together to music, and the children learn a routine. All students will be assessed in the first weeks of classes and may be moved to a different level. Bodysuit and shorts are preferred. Students will dance barefoot.
Instructor: Sydney Poland

title: Night at the Theatre: Swan Lake (New Westminster)
description:
Join us for a night at Massey Theatre! Imagine the haunting elegance of Swan Lake, but instead of a far-off European kingdom, the tragedy unfolds against the rugged, misty shores of the Fortress of Louisbourg, Nova Scotia. For Ballet Jörgen’s 25th anniversary, the company’s Artistic Director and CEO Bengt Jörgen re-visioned the classical and dramatic Swan Lake, adding a hint of Canadian heritage (ticket included in fee). Before the show, have tea and a light snack supporting local Dolce Amore (not included in the fee). Pickup only at Confederation. Drop off will be at Eileen Dailly Pool.
Last day for refund is on January 27th.

title: Reserve In Advance: Pickleball Adult
description:
*Note this program is a 1/4 court and one net*Please arrive early and check in at the gymnasium to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation.
Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program.

title: Compound Lifting - Part 1: Deadlifts & Squats
description:
Learn the fundamentals of compound lifting and see the benefits! This three-part training program focuses on learning, practicing, and mastering the big 6 compound exercises (squats, deadlifts, bench press, overhead press, bent over row and pull ups). Learn the correct muscle groups to use, proper form, and modifications for each exercise. By training multiple muscle groups at once you will burn calories, improve intramuscular connection, core strength, balance, functional strength, muscular strength, and build more muscle mass along the way.
This is part 1 of a three-part compound lifting program. This session focuses on mastering squats and deadlifts. Knowing the correct form for squats and deadlifts is essential for feeling more comfortable in the gym. If you’ve ever asked yourself; how low should I squat? How can I do a deadlift without my lower back getting involved? Can my knees pass my toes? What muscles should I be feeling? You are in the right place! Our knowledgeable instructor will guide you through how to move properly through both a squat and conventional deadlift while providing helpful tips and guidance along the way to ensure you are confident about each exercise.
Completion of the PAR-Q+ form is required to participate.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program.

title: National Lifeguard Pool
description:
The NL Pool certification is designed to develop the fundamental values, judgment, knowledge, skills and fitness required by lifeguards. This course emphasizes the lifeguarding skills, principles and practices, and the decision-making processes that assist the lifeguard in providing effective safety supervision in swimming pool environments. Prerequisite: Bronze Cross (does not need to be current) and Standard First Aid or Aquatic Emergency Care (current award recommended) by the first day of the NL course. Emergency First Aid certificates obtained in high school are not accepted. Must be 15 years old by the last day of the course. Alert Manual is required and not included in fee. There is a non-refundable exam fee.
Students must be prepared to bring bathing suit, manual and paper for each class. Candidates will need to provide proof of the prerequisites on the 1st day of the course to the instructor or be sent home with no refund. Emergency First Aid certificates obtained in high school are not accepted. Recognized Agencies for Standard First Aid or Aquatic Emergency Care are: any Canadian branch of the Lifesaving Society, Canadian Red Cross, St John Ambulance, Canadian Heart and Stroke Foundation or Canadian Ski Patrol. 100% attendance is required.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures.

title: Adult 1
description: You’ll work towards 10-15m swim on your front and back. You’ll learn safe entries into shallow and deep water, develop skills while wearing a PFD, and learn breath control and underwater skills. Floats, glides, flutter kick and vertical whip kick are introduced. Your fitness will improve through interval training and learning how to perform front crawl and back crawl.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Bronze Medallion
description: Prerequisites: Must be 13 years old OR have Bronze Star. Understand the lifesaving principles embodied in the four components of water rescue education: judgment, knowledge, skill and fitness. Rescuers learn self rescue techniques, defence and release methods, and tows and carries in preparation for challenging rescues involving conscious and unconscious victims of various types, including spinal injuries and circulatory emergencies. Lifesavers develop stroke efficiency and endurance in a timed swim. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.

title: Reserve In Advance: Table Tennis All Ages
description:
Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. For all ages programs, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. For all ages programs, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Ceramics 1: Introduction
description:
Designed especially for absolute beginners who learn a range of basic methods used in making clay forms by hand and on the wheel. Learn glazing and decorating techniques. title: Ceramics 2: Refining Handbuilding
description:
Slow precision describes the process and possibilities of handbuilding with clay. This new course offers intermediate and advanced techniques for working on larger and more complex ceramic forms. You will learn to create templates and simple bisque molds, and develop strategies for adding lids and handles to your work. Projects include a curved-sided box, large coiled vessels, and a kurinuki (carved) tray. Clay is not included in course fee. Students must purchase clay ticket from Front Office. Prerequisite: Ceramics 1: Introduction or Handbuilt Sculptural Techniques, or equivalent experience. Students must have some proficiency with basic handbuilding, including rolling coils and slabs. This course is not suitable for beginners. Instructor: Fredi Rahn
Learn more about Fredi

title: Ceramics 3: From The Ashes
description:
In this advanced specialty course, ceramic artist Cheryl Stapleton will lead participants through designing and preparing pots for sawdust, loading and firing the kiln, and then unloading and polishing the final pieces. Participants will form pots by hand or on the wheel, then burnish or apply terra sigillata to the surfaces. After bisque, the pots will be loaded and fired in the sawdust kiln with organic materials to create soft variations of colour on the surfaces of the works. Over 5 sessions, participants will complete 1 sawdust firing. Tools and clay not included in course fee. Students must purchase C-3 clay ticket from Front Office prior to start of class. This course is not suitable for beginners. No refunds after January 4. Mandatory attendance for the loading and unloading dates. The loading and firing of the sawdust kiln will happen on February 9. The kiln unload will happen on February 16.
Learn more about Cheryl

title: Ceramics 3: From The Ashes
description: In this advanced specialty course, ceramic artist Cheryl Stapleton will lead participants through designing and preparing pots for sawdust, loading and firing the kiln, and then unloading and polishing the final pieces. Participants will form pots by hand or on the wheel, then burnish or apply terra sigillata to the surfaces. After bisque, the pots will be loaded and fired in the sawdust kiln with organic materials to create soft variations of colour on the surfaces of the works. Over 5 sessions, participants will complete 1 sawdust firing. Tools and clay not included in course fee. Students must purchase C-3 clay ticket from Front Office prior to start of class. This course is not suitable for beginners. No refunds after February 8. Mandatory attendance for the loading and unloading dates. The loading and firing of the sawdust kiln will happen on March 16. The kiln unload will happen on March 23.

title: Ceramics 3: Glaze Fundamentals
description:
This course provides an introduction to the basics of glaze theory. Over six weeks, the course will explore glaze chemistry through lectures, demonstrations, and lab work under the guidance of ceramic artist Mitra Mahmoodi. Although the focus will be on cone 6 glazes, the principles learned can be applied to all firing temperatures. Participants will learn to mix test batches, create formulas, line blend, and fire glazes daily. By mapping results on the Stull chart, participants will gain insights into manipulating glaze chemistry to develop new glazes. Additionally, the course will address common glaze defects and their solutions. Topics such as the ceramic periodic table, using the Stull map, working with glazy.org, and finding and adjusting a true cone 6 glaze to suit your preferences will also be covered. This activity is not suitable for beginners. Clay included in course fee. All registrants must bring their own N95 mask or respirator to the start of class. No refunds after January 18.
Learn more about Mitra

title: Bronze Medallion
description: Prerequisites: Must be 13 years old OR have Bronze Star. Understand the lifesaving principles embodied in the four components of water rescue education: judgment, knowledge, skill and fitness. Rescuers learn self rescue techniques, defence and release methods, and tows and carries in preparation for challenging rescues involving conscious and unconscious victims of various types, including spinal injuries and circulatory emergencies. Lifesavers develop stroke efficiency and endurance in a timed swim. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. There is a non-refundable exam fee. 100% attendance is recommended.

title: Bronze Cross
description: Prerequisite: 13yrs +up and Bronze Medallion. Designed for lifesavers who want the challenge of more advanced training, including an introduction to safety supervision in aquatic facilities. Swimmers develop proficiency at performing patient assessments, managing aquatic spinal injuries and preventing loss of life in a variety of aquatic emergencies, while developing stroke endurance and fitness training skills. Is one of the prerequisite awards for all advanced Lifeguarding and Leadership training programs. It is also worth two Grade 11 high school credits. Canadian Life Saving Manual is required. description: This is a satellite program operated by the ceramics staff at the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, City of Burnaby's internationally renowned ceramic arts facility. Steeped in tradition and innovation, the teapot is one of the most fundamental ceramic forms, yet one of the most challenging to perfect. Potter and educator Fredi Rahn will guide participants through artful design and technical consideration for building delightful, handbuilt teapots. This is an intermediate level course and not suitable for beginners. Must be proficient with coils and slab-building. Participants will spend the first three sessions making their forms and the final session glazing. The instructor will arrange a separate pick-up date for finished pieces. Clay and supplies included in course fee. Due to the design of this course, no withdrawals/refunds after January 18. No class February 16.

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Elisabeta Podut
description:
Students can sign up for private piano lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: Elisabeta Podut.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details.- Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Swimmer 6
description: Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 5. These swimmers will become proficient at deep water skills including stride entries and compact jumps. They’ll develop lifesaving kicks such as eggbeater and scissor kick. Breaststroke, front crawl, and back crawl are further developed. Head-up swims, interval training and a 300m workout develop strength and endurance. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.25 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 6
description: Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 5. These swimmers will become proficient at deep water skills including stride entries and compact jumps. They’ll develop lifesaving kicks such as eggbeater and scissor kick. Breaststroke, front crawl, and back crawl are further developed. Head-up swims, interval training and a 300m workout develop strength and endurance. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.25 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program.

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Blacksmithing Level 2: Simple Scrolls
description:
In Simple Scrolls, you’ll refine your blacksmithing skills while creating a functional and decorative piece with intricate scrollwork. Craft a brooch, hair pin, a candle holder, or a tea towel rack, all incorporating elegant scrolling designs. This course offers a perfect opportunity to deepen your metalworking expertise while making beautiful, handmade items. Leave with your own crafted pieces and a stronger command of blacksmithing techniques.
This Level 2 workshop is considered an intermediate blacksmithing course. Successful completion of the course fulfills the prerequisite for taking BVM's Level 3 courses.
Online registration is not available for this course. To register please call 604-297-4565.
Cancellations within 48 hours of the start of the course will not be issued a refund.

description:
This introduction to blacksmithing starts with learning the importance of safety in a blacksmith's shop. The hands-on component has students lighting a coal forge, as well as making a coat hook and dinner triangle. Students will learn how to heat mild steel in a forge and shape it with a hammer and anvil. Steel-toed boots recommended.
This Level 1 workshop is considered an introductory blacksmithing course. Successful completion of the course fulfills the prerequisite for taking BVM's Level 2 courses.
Cancellations within 48 hours of the start of the course will not be issued a refund.

description:
This extended course is for students who would like a more in-depth introduction to blacksmithing. The hands-on component has students lighting a coal forge, as well as making a coat hook, dinner triangle and striker. Get started on your new blacksmithing hobby with information on what equipment is needed, how and where to get it, and the differences between coal and propane forges. Steel-toed boots recommended.
This Level 1 workshop is considered an introductory blacksmithing course. Successful completion of the course fulfills the prerequisite for taking BVM's Level 2 courses.
Cancellations within 48 hours of the start of the course will not be issued a refund.

title: At the Forge Level 0: Copper Rose
description:
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll create a stunning rose using metal shears to cut out petals, which you’ll then rivet onto a beautifully forged copper stem. With a torch and pliers, you’ll shape the petals into a lifelike rose.No prior experience is needed. Join us and craft a timeless token of your affection that won’t wilt, no matter how much time passes.
This Level 0 workshop does not fulfill the prerequisite for taking further blacksmithing programs with BVM. Please register for an introductory Level 1 course, if you wish to continue learning.
Cancellations made within 48 hours of the start of the program will not be issued a refund.

Students with no forging experience must complete an introductory workshop (Basic, Immersion, or Forging for Youth) before enrolling in this course. Steel-toed boots are recommended.

title: Introduction to Figure Drawing
description:
Ideal course for anyone looking to begin studying and drawing the human figure whether you are a complete beginner or looking to strengthen your foundational drawing skills. Learn to observe and represent the human figure through the study of basic body proportions, gesture, anatomy, and the use of light and shadow. Through guided exercises, you will develop your ability to capture movement, explore form, and create dynamic and expressive compositions. Working from live models and printed references, you will gain a deeper understanding of the human form, learning to translate its shapes, gestures and subtleties onto paper.
This course encourages curiousity, experimentation, and careful observation, providing a welcoming environment in which to build confidence and develop your personal approach to figure drawing. Instructor: Alex GreghiModel fee for 3 sessions included in course fee. No Class February 15. See STUDENT SUPPLY LIST in Notes section below.

title: Paint: Explorations: Acrylics
description:
Acrylic paint offers a wide range of expressive possibilities, from soft, watercolour-like washes to thick, richly textured, and energetic applications. We’ll explore primary, secondary, and tertiary colours, deepening our understanding of the colour wheel while experimenting with a variety of painting surfaces, including raw and primed canvas, heavy paper, wood, and lightweight papers. Exploring the relationship between form and background through colour, scale, and composition will be another key part of our process. We’ll also create multilayered, collage-inspired works incorporating drawing techniques, playful experimentation, and individual expression. This eight-week painting adventure offers a rich, creative experience, encouraging each participant to discover new approaches, explore materials, and develop their own unique artistic voice.
Instructor: Eleanor Hannan
$10 fee for some supplies. See STUDENT SUPPLY LIST in Notes section below for additional items to be purchased.

description:
Children are given the opportunity to thrive by developing and building upon their innate artistic instincts and imagination. Instructors provide guidance and encouragement with fun projects and tons of different art materials to explore. title: Painting for Tweens
description:
Students explore painting techniques and materials, especially designed to develop creative ability through a blend of instruction, freedom of expression and individual attention. Wear clothes that are suitable for art activities. $10.00 extra visual arts material fee applicable.
Instructor: Mat Holmstrom
ageText: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 14 yrs,

title: Abstract Art: Drawing & Painting
description:
This course introduces abstract art as a way of exploring ideas, emotions, and experiences through drawing and painting. Participants will experiment with colour, line, shape, texture, gesture, and composition to discover new possibilities for artistic expressions.
Through guided exercises and independent exploration, participants will investigate how everyday observations, memories, and personal experiences can be transformed into abstract visual forms. The course emphasizes curiosity, experimentation, and the development of a personal approach to abstraction.
Instructor: Mahsa Farzi
See STUDENT SUPPLY LIST in Notes section below. NO CLASS: Feb 15th.

title: Creative Drawing
description:
This course approaches drawing as an open-ended space for experimentation, discovery, and personal expression. Participants will explore different ways of making marks, developing images, and responding to the world around them. Through playful exercises, creative prompts, and material exploration, participants will experiment with observation, imagination, memory, intuition, and chance. The course encourages curiosity, risk-taking and the development of an individual visual language.
Instructor: Mahsa Farzi

title: Dye, Print & Paint on Fabric
description:
Note: Change in time and fee from printed Activity Guide. Discover the many ways colour can meet cloth. In this hands-on course, you’ll explore Shibori, the Japanese art of creating patterns through folding, binding, and clamping fabric before dyeing, alongside alternative approaches to painting and printing on textiles. Experiment with fabric paints, stamping, stencils, and found-object printing, then learn to layer and combine techniques to build rich, one-of-a-kind surfaces. Create a collection of sample pieces and finished fabrics ready for sewing, framing, or wearing. All levels welcome; no experience needed.
Instructor: Mariana FrochtengartenFabric dyes, pigments, blank scarf, and some fabric included in $30 extra fee. Some additional supplies needed, See STUDENT SUPPLY LIST in NOTES section below.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program.

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha / Core
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered with an emphasis on the core muscles.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Reserve In Advance: Yoga Hatha
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. This classical form of yoga is a rejuvenating practice that releases tension from the muscles accumulated in everyday life and sports activities. Learn to breathe deeply while experiencing a variety of postures to stimulate the body physically and mentally. Through this practice you enhance flexibility, increase muscle tone and concentration, detoxify the organs and feel a state of deep relaxation. A variation of poses will be offered.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Intro to Gliders
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Gliders skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

description: Designed for those who want to improve their speed, agility, power and control while getting a great workout! A CSA-approved hockey helmet and full hockey equipment are mandatory for all participants. Please bring your own stick. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description: Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.00.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description: Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description: Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description: Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star.

Pre-requisite: Youth I or an evaluation. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. Helmets are available to borrow no charge. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register in more than one lesson set at a time.
ageText: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 18 yrs,

title: Blades 1
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Blades skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. In this level, children learn about safety on the ice, how to fall down and stand up, walk on the ice without assistance and are introduced to stopping, gliding and sculling. By the end of this level children need to be able to skate the width of the rink with confidence using both feet along with demonstrating other building blocks. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs,

title: Gliders 1
description: In this beginner level, children work on building confidence and speed while being introduced to gliding, stopping and backward skating. Prerequisite: Intro to Gliders or an evaluation. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.
ageText: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs,

title: Skating Lessons: Parent & Tot Adult Participation
description: Join us for our skate lesson program designed to make your child's experience on ice a positive one. Our instructor will work with you and your child to develop their basic skating skills using games and activities. Maximum of 1 child per adult. A CSA approved hockey or snow sport helmet is mandatory for both adult and child in this program. All children must be accompanied on the ice by an adult on skates or ice cleats. Skate and helmet rental are included in the program price. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.
ageText: Age at least 2 yrs but less than 6 yrs,

title: Axe Capoeira - Brazilian Martial Arts
description: We are now excited to offer a Capoeira course to introduce your child to the basic fundamentals of the art form. This starter course will cover basic kicks, movements, and acrobatics, as well as teaching you basic music skills and about the history of Capoeira. We will also cover the correct techniques to prepare you physically to transition into the next level of classes.
