title: Axe Capoeira - Brazilian Martial Arts
description: Capoeira is an Afro-Brazilian martial art that combines music, self-defense, dance, acrobatics and physical conditioning to create a unique, multidisciplinary experience. Modern capoeira is one of the most inherently diverse martial arts in the world today with creativity, music, self-expression and strategic thinking as much a part of the core curriculum as physical training and fitness. Kids ages 7-13 yrs old will love this program.

title: Reserve In Advance: Table Tennis All Ages
description:
Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. For all ages, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Please arrive earl and check in at the front counter to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Video Memoir
description:
Every life is a collection of unique, unforgettable chapters. How will you share yours?
This creative, hands-on workshop helps you transform your personal memories into a professionally filmed legacy.
In the first half of the course, you will engage in guided writing exercises to uncover, structure, and polish meaningful stories from your life.
In the second half, you will step in front of the camera to film your stories with gentle, professional guidance.
At the end of the term, you will receive a digital video copy of your memoir to share with family, friends, and future generations.
No prior writing or video experience is required.
Instructor: Orsy Szabo

title: Photography: From Ordinary to Wow!
description:
SIMPLE TIPS TO MAKE YOUR PHOTOS MORE INTERESTING Whether you’re sharing your adventures on your phone, creating a scrapbook, or simply building a collection of wonderful memories, it all starts with taking photos you’re proud of. And often, great photos are simply about where you stand, what you include, and how you frame the scene.
In this fun, practical workshop, you’ll learn easy composition tips to take your photos from ordinary to eye-catching. Through plenty of examples, simple ideas, and a little laughter, you’ll discover how small changes can make a surprisingly big difference. Learn to see your surroundings differently and create photos that tell the story of your travels in the best way possible.
Whatever camera you use, these tips are for you! This is not a technical class—we won’t get bogged down in complicated camera settings or technical jargon. Just bring your camera, your curiosity, and a willingness to see things a little differently.
Instructor Jillian Chateauneuf is a professional photographer who has spent years behind the camera—and now travels exclusively with her iPhone.

title: Siu Mai Making Lab Workshop
description: Discover the art of dim sum by making your own siu mai from scratch. In this hands-on workshop, participants learn to prepare a savoury pork and shrimp filling with mushrooms, then fold and shape the open-topped dumplings in thin yellow wrappers before steaming them to perfection. Everyone gets to enjoy freshly steamed siu mai on the spot and takes home some to share, plus a recipe card to recreate them at home. No cooking experience required — this session is for children, youth, and families. Children under 12 must be registered with an adult. Led by Abraham Wong, a Hong Kong-born, Vancouver-based chef featured by CBC Vancouver for his Mid-Autumn mooncake teaching.

title: Lunar New Year Dumplings Workshop
description: Ring in the Lunar New Year with a family dumpling-making session. Dumplings are a festive favourite, shaped like ancient gold ingots and said to bring wealth and good fortune in the year ahead. In this hands-on workshop, participants learn to fill and fold their own dumplings with a choice of vegetable or pork and chive filling, then taste some freshly cooked. No cooking experience required - this session is for children, youth, and families. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. Led by Abraham Wong, a Hong Kong-born, Vancouver-based chef featured by CBC Vancouver for his Mid-Autumn mooncake teaching.

Patrons are limited to registering for a maximum of two Open Workshops per week (Monday-Sunday) and will be withdrawn from Open Workshops that exceed the maximum limit.

title: Reserve In Advance: Total Body Conditioning
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. Use your body weight, and equipment to improve your functional core strength with exercises that focus on your abs, back and more. No cardio component in this class.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Jr Golf | FUNdamentals (age 5-7) | Skill Development
description:
Level 2: Building Skills & Confidence — Advancing Your Child’s Golf Game
This 4-week program is designed for young golfers ready to build on the basics and take their skills to the next level. Through engaging practice sessions, kids will refine their putting, chipping, and full swings while learning key aspects of golf rules and etiquette. It’s a great way to boost confidence, improve technique, and deepen their understanding of the game — all in a fun and supportive setting.
Program Details:
  • Duration: 4 sessions (45 minutes each)
  • Equipment: Golf clubs provided if needed, so there’s no need to purchase equipment
  • Weather: Sessions run rain or shine, with access to a covered, heated practice range

Cancellation Policy:
  • Cancellations require a 7-day notice for a full refund

This program is ideal for kids who have some golf experience or have completed the beginner level and are excited to keep progressing. Our friendly coaches help each child develop their skills at their own pace, fostering a positive learning environment that encourages growth and a lifelong love for golf.
Help your child strengthen their skills and passion for golf — sign up today!

Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. Reserve in advance is now available for the sports of Squash.

One court booking is 45 minutes. There is a limit of 2 court time slots per day. Maximum 3 players are allowed per court. One participant is required to book the court. The 2 additional players invited to play will need to pay at the time of check-in.

Check-in at the front desk to receive wristband is required before entering the courts.

There are two dedicated Squash courts (court #1 and court #2)

There is a Reserve In Advance Squash Challenge Program on Saturdays and Sundays except statutory holiday weekends. Program capacity is 11 spots. Each participant needs to register their spot. Join a player run recreational game of squash in a round robin style of play.

Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in-person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. Participants may lose their spot if they are 10 minutes or more late.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

prices.description: Child (12-14 yrs) fee for up to 14 years old
Youth (15-25 yrs) fee for 15 up to 25 years old
Adult (26-64 yrs) fee for 26 up to 64 years old
Senior (65+ yrs) fee for 65 or more years old

One court booking is 45 minutes. There is a limit of 2 court time slots per day. Maximum 3 players are allowed per court. One participant is required to book the court. The 2 additional players invited to play will need to pay at the time of check-in.

Check-in at the front desk to receive wristband is required before entering the courts.

There are two dedicated Squash courts (court #1 and court #2)

There is a Reserve In Advance Squash Challenge Program on Saturdays and Sundays except statutory holiday weekends. Program capacity is 11 spots. Each participant needs to register their spot. Join a player run recreational game of squash in a round robin style of play.

Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in-person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. Participants may lose their spot if they are 10 minutes or more late.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

One court booking is 45 minutes. There is a limit of 2 court time slots per day. Maximum 3 players are allowed per court. One participant is required to book the court. The 2 additional players invited to play will need to pay at the time of check-in.

Check-in at the front desk to receive wristband is required before entering the courts.

There are two dedicated Squash courts (court #1 and court #2)

There is a Reserve In Advance Squash Challenge Program on Saturdays and Sundays except statutory holiday weekends. Program capacity is 11 spots. Each participant needs to register their spot. Join a player run recreational game of squash in a round robin style of play.

Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in-person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. Participants may lose their spot if they are 10 minutes or more late.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

One court booking is 45 minutes. There is a limit of 2 court time slots per day. Maximum 3 players are allowed per court. One participant is required to book the court. The 2 additional players invited to play will need to pay at the time of check-in.

Check-in at the front desk to receive wristband is required before entering the courts.

There are two dedicated Squash courts (court #1 and court #2)

There is a Reserve In Advance Squash Challenge Program on Saturdays and Sundays except statutory holiday weekends. Program capacity is 11 spots. Each participant needs to register their spot. Join a player run recreational game of squash in a round robin style of play.

Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in-person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. Participants may lose their spot if they are 10 minutes or more late.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

One court booking is 45 minutes. There is a limit of 2 court time slots per day. Maximum 3 players are allowed per court. One participant is required to book the court. The 2 additional players invited to play will need to pay at the time of check-in.

Check-in at the front desk to receive wristband is required before entering the courts.

There are two dedicated Squash courts (court #1 and court #2)

There is a Reserve In Advance Squash Challenge Program on Saturdays and Sundays except statutory holiday weekends. Program capacity is 11 spots. Each participant needs to register their spot. Join a player run recreational game of squash in a round robin style of play.

Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. Please arrive early to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in-person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. Participants may lose their spot if they are 10 minutes or more late.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

Check-in at the front desk to receive wristband is required before entering the courts.

There are two dedicated Squash courts (court #1 and court #2)

There is a Reserve In Advance Squash Challenge Program on Saturdays and Sundays except statutory holiday weekends. Program capacity is 11 spots. Each participant needs to register their spot. Join a player run recreational game of squash in a round robin style of play.

Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in-person drop-in, subject to remaining availability. Participants may lose their spot if they are 10 minutes or more late.

Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.

If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Active Aging: Yoga for Movement Disorders
description:
This yoga class has been developed for people with a movement disorder that makes it challenging to engage in basic yoga movements. The class is suitable for patrons with Parkinson’s disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Tourette syndrome, and other medical conditions that restrict movement and affect muscle strength, flexibility and balance including stroke recovery and surgery. Students are encouraged to join at their own pace. If students require one-to-one support, we require caregivers to attend and join in the program where needed. Please wear comfortable clothing, bring a bottle of water and a yoga mat.
Instructor: Jane

title: Choose to Move™ Information Session
description:
Join Choose to Moveto help introduce the habit of physical activity into your daily life in ways that make sense for you. Choose to Move is free and flexible, and provides you with motivation and support to become more active. In Choose to Move, you receive both individual and group support. You will work with a trained activity coach to develop and stick to a physical activity plan made just for you. You choose activities that you know you will enjoy and are able to do! You will also join a group of other Choose to Movers to share successes and challenges. With the help of your activity coach & and support group, you will find the motivation and accountability you need to achieve your goals.

Register by contacting Bonsor 55+ at 604-297-4580 or for more information.

title: Choose to Move™
description:
Choose to Moveis a free 3-month motivational coaching program for older adults wishing to become more physically active and to help introduce the habit of physical activity into your daily life in ways that makes sense for you. Choose to Move is free and flexible, and provides you with motivation along your journey to become more active. In Choose to Move, you receive both individual and group support. You will work with a trained activity coach to develop and stick to a physical activity plan made just for you. You choose activities that you know you will enjoy and are able to do! You will also join a group of other Choose to Movers to share successes and challenges. With the help of your activity coach & and support group, you will find the motivation and accountability you need to achieve your goals.

Register by contacting Bonsor 55+ at 604-297-45980 or for more information.

title: ActivAge™
description: ActivAge™ is a free 3-month group-led physical activity program for inactive older adults. It introduces participants to physical activity and reinforces their commitment to incorporate it into their daily lives. The program is progressive with planned physical activities (stretching, activity, and cool-down) based on ActivAge™ training. This fun and social program will help get participants moving in a relaxed environment with likeminded people. The program focuses on improving activities associated with daily living, strengthening muscles used day-to-day (ie: bending, lifting, stretching, etc). Each class incorporates physical activities that engage participants, and features in-class discussions and resources to improve overall health and physical well being. New Registration for ActivAge™ is just open to those registered in the Choose to Move program. This program runs Tuesdays. Please call Bonsor 55+ to register at 604-297-4580 and for more information.

This class is designed for runners with a consistent base, for those who can run 10K nonstop or 5K in under 30 minutes. Building on the foundations introduced in the Beginner program, this program entails extended runs and higher-intensity sessions to further develop endurance and performance.
*It’s recommended that you complete the Running for Beginners program before registering for the Intermediate class.
*Please meet in the lobby at Eileen Dailly. The group will head to the track together. If you are running late, head to Confederation track. Bring a water bottle, wear comfortable shoes and clothing. This program will run rain or shine.

title: Blades 1
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Blades skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. In this level, children learn about safety on the ice, how to fall down and stand up, walk on the ice without assistance and are introduced to stopping, gliding and sculling. By the end of this level children need to be able to skate the width of the rink with confidence using both feet along with demonstrating other building blocks. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Guitar, Bass, or Ukulele: Private Lesson Long-Term Craig M
description:
Students can sign up for private lessons in guitar, bass guitar or ukulele from fall through spring. Students must provide their own instrument. Instructor: Craig McCaul.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

description: Prerequisite: age: 24-36 months. Parent & Tot 3 teaches toddlers how to safely enter the water wearing a PFD. title: Reserve In Advance: Zumba®
description:
Reserve in advance is available for this activity. (All levels/moderate) Zumba® is an exciting fusion of Latin music and aerobic fitness that is sure to have you enjoying your workout and dancing away your worries!
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

description: Registered classPerfect for our younger Zumba® fans! Kids 4-6 years old get the chance to socialize with friends and jam out to their favorite music. description:

title: Reserve In Advance: Pilates
description:

Then we progress into the structure of Pilates to train and strengthen the core, so that we move more fluidly and with less effort in our lives.

title: Reserve In Advance: Table Tennis All Ages
description:
Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. For all ages, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Please arrive earl and check in at the front counter to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Cantonese Tour: Jiangang Su, A Thousand Years in One Stream
description:
Join us on Sunday, December 20th for a free guided exhibition tour of Jiangang Su's exhibition, A Thousand Years in One Stream, in Cantonese and Mandarin!
Tours are 30 minutes long.
12:30-1pm – Tour in Cantonese
1-1:30pm – Tour in Mandarin
Ten years ago, Jiangang Su moved to Canada. As he first settled in Burnaby, he was confronted with the quiet depths of this place—taking tranquil walks on the shores of Deer Lake, experiencing a world of timeless waterways co-existing with a city projecting itself into the future. With extensive training in traditional Chinese ink wash and gongbi painting, Su projects his practice towards contemporary calligraphy, where delicate branches and flowing streams emanate breath, movement and the persistence of each moment.
Free to attend, no registration required. For more information, call 604-297-4422 (English only).

As he first settled in Burnaby, he was confronted with the quiet depths of this place—taking tranquil walks on the shores of Deer Lake, experiencing a world of timeless waterways co-existing with a city projecting itself into the future. With extensive training in traditional Chinese ink wash and gongbi painting, Su projects his practice towards contemporary calligraphy, where delicate branches and flowing streams emanate breath, movement and the persistence of each moment.
Free to attend, no registration required. For more information, call 604-297-4422 (English only).

title: Jr Golf | FUNdamentals (age 5-7) | Skill Development
description:
Level 2: Building Skills & Confidence — Advancing Your Child’s Golf Game
This 4-week program is designed for young golfers ready to build on the basics and take their skills to the next level. Through engaging practice sessions, kids will refine their putting, chipping, and full swings while learning key aspects of golf rules and etiquette. It’s a great way to boost confidence, improve technique, and deepen their understanding of the game — all in a fun and supportive setting.
Program Details:
  • Duration: 4 sessions (45 minutes each)
  • Equipment: Golf clubs provided if needed, so there’s no need to purchase equipment
  • Weather: Sessions run rain or shine, with access to a covered, heated practice range

Cancellation Policy:
  • Cancellations require a 7-day notice for a full refund

This program is ideal for kids who have some golf experience or have completed the beginner level and are excited to keep progressing. Our friendly coaches help each child develop their skills at their own pace, fostering a positive learning environment that encourages growth and a lifelong love for golf.
Help your child strengthen their skills and passion for golf — sign up today!

title: Ballet: Beginner Continuing - Adult
description:
Ballet classes focus on developing alignment, strength, coordination and expressivity using the fundamentals of dance technique. Classes are taught in a supportive environment . This continuing level is geared to dancers with at least one year of dance experience and are wanting to transition to the intermediate levels. No Drop-ins.
Instructor: Jullianna Oke
REFUND POLICYYou'll receive a full refund if the activity is cancelled or if you request a refund at least 7 days before the start of the activity. If your request comes less than 7 days before the activity starts, there is a 10% refund fee on the original price you paid.
After the activity has started, refunds are pro-rated according to the number of sessions remaining and a 10% refund fee will be applied. No refunds will be granted after the third session has ended.
Note: There may be exceptions to these cancellation and refund guidelines as noted in the activity description. Please check your receipt.

description:
Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. For all ages, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Please arrive earl and check in at the front counter to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

You'll make five hot and chilled holiday appetizers: creamy mushroom and thyme tartlets, cranberry-beet mousse cucumber cups, hot coronation chicken puffs, Cantonese shrimp toast and baked mini potatoes with salmon and dill.
All equipment and food is supplied.

description:
Join Abraham Wong from Bow to Plates as he teaches your child everything they need to know about making and creating a Japanese Sando.

All equipment and food is supplied.

title: Adult Golf: Learn to Play - Putt, Chip, Pitch and Swing
description:
This 2-lesson series introduces the skills and basic understanding needed to start enjoying the game of golf. These lessons focus on building the golf swing and learning to putt and chip with your golf instructor. These lessons teach you golf terminology, equipment needs, rules, etiquette and scorekeeping.
Sessions 1 - 2 are held at Burnaby Mountain Golf Course (90 mins),
All equipment is provided but if you have it, bring your own.
6 per class maximum. 4 minimum.
Classes are conducted rain or shine.
Class cancellation / refund policy: 7 days notice is required for cancellation and refund.

title: Jr Golf | Play (age 8-10) | Beginner
description:
This beginner 4-week program introduces putting, chipping, and full swing. A focused 4-week program that builds solid fundamentals in Aim, Posture, Grip, and Swing Motion, plus the key putting, chipping, and full-swing skills that help young golfers progress quickly.
Level: Beginner
Number of Classes: 4
Class Duration: 60 mins each
Min/Max number of participants: 6
Rental clubs available
Classes are conducted in rain or shine.
Class cancellation / refund policy: 7 days' notice is required for cancellation and refund.

title: The Pleasure of Play
description:
Rediscover the infectious joy of connection and play!

Experience the freedom and empowerment of becoming fully present and alive. Shift your perspective on making mistakes and discover the pleasure of sharing yourself with others and being witnessed in all your glorious, messy humanity.

This workshop explores clown and mask work as accessible gateways to help participants activate and share this state of joy and play.

Open to both newcomers and experienced performers.

Instructor: Sonia Norris

Sonia Norris has been teaching acting internationally for 30 years, specializing in mask, play, clown, and devised ensemble creation. She trained with renowned teachers of physical theatre at Ecole Jacques Lecoq in France, Ecole Philippe Gaulier in England/France, Dell ‘Arte School of Physical Theatre in California, and most recently with master clown Angela de Castro in London and mask teacher Matteo Destro in Italy.

She is a graduate of the Playhouse Acting School in Vancouver and received her MFA in Directing from York University. As a director and creator, Sonia has toured productions to the Arctic, South Africa, Zimbabwe, the Yukon, across Canada, and the United States and has extensive experience working with international companies including Handspring Puppet Company, Stratford Shakespeare Festival, Luminato Festival, Harare International Festival of the Arts, Rogue Artists Ensemble, Cirqiniq, Balancing on the Edge, Caravan Farm Theatre, Crows Theatre, Nightwood Theatre, Banff Centre Indigenous Dance, Red Sky Performance, and LEGacy Circus.

Currently, she is the Head of Acting/Associate Professor of Acting in the Theatre Department at California State University Northridge in Los Angeles, and the Founding Artistic Director of the Circus & Clown Desert Intensive in Las Vegas.

In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Skating Lessons: Adapted
description: For children with developmental and/or physical disabilities who haven't yet learned to skate or for skaters who need some extra support. Participants are exposed to a wide variety of skills based on their ability. Ratio is two instructors to three participants. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. Please do not register for more than one lesson set at a time. If you require skate rentals, please purchase punch cards on or before the first day of lessons.
ageText: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 13 yrs,

title: Intro to Hockey
description: This exciting class introduces the fundamentals of ice hockey while improving skating speed, balance and control. Stick-handling, shooting, passing and drills will be incorporated to make sessions challenging and fun. Helmet with face cage, hockey gloves and a stick are required. (Full hockey equipment is optional). For children currently skating at a GLIDERS 2 / BLADES 2 level or higher. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons.

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Debbie Lin
description:
Students can sign up for private piano lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: TBA.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Reserve In Advance: Aquafit
description:
Set your own pace! Improve cardiovascular fitness, increase strength and tone muscles. Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation. Please arrive early and stay until the end of the class to ensure safety and enjoyment for everyone. Participants arriving 5 minutes after class start time will not be admitted. Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Standard First Aid (for Adults)
description: ADULT PROGRAM. Participants please contact Alvin Cheung or Carson Croy before registering. This course is the most comprehensive first aid training program for the general public and is a prerequisite for the National Lifeguard program. Rescuers are trained in the skills and knowledge needed to assess and provide basic life support to patients with airway, breathing or circulatory emergencies, as well as how to manage medical, musculoskeletal and environmental emergencies. Includes CPR-C certification. Canadian First Aid Manual is required and not included in fee. Purchase at front desk. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $30.00. 100% attendance is required.

title: Butoh Workshop with Salome Nieto
description:
Participants will begin with gentle physical warm-up exercises to awaken the body, develop awareness, and release physical tension.Through guided imagery, improvisation, and sensory exploration, they will be invited to let go of habitual movement patterns and personal expectations. The session explores the dissolution of the ego and a state of openness and receptivity in which participants allow images, sensations, and imagination to guide their movement. No previous Butoh experience is necessary; curiosity and openness to exploration are all that is needed.
REFUND POLICY You'll receive a full refund if the activity is cancelled or if you request a refund at least 7 days before the start of the activity. If your request comes less than 7 days before the activity starts, there is a 10% refund fee on the original price you paid. After the activity has started, refunds are pro-rated according to the number of sessions remaining and a 10% refund fee will be applied. No refunds will be granted after the third session has ended.Note: There may be exceptions to these cancellation and refund guidelines as noted in the activity description. Please check your receipt.

  • NOTE: an orientation is NOT a personal training session.
  • Schedules are subject to change.

The goal of the weight room orientation is to provide someone new to exercise or new to the facility a basic introduction to the weight room.

  • A 30 minute safety weight room orientation. Participants will receive training on: safe practices in the weight room, proper use of equipment and a review of policies and etiquette.
  • We will provide you with the basics of how to use weight and cardio equipment. You will learn how to start, stop and change settings on cardio machines, change seat height and weight selections on machines, and have a discussion of proper form on the weight machines.
  • All instructors are experienced and certified.
  • NOTE: an orientation is NOT a personal training session.
  • Schedules are subject to change.

title: Blades 1
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Blades skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. In this level, children learn about safety on the ice, how to fall down and stand up, walk on the ice without assistance and are introduced to stopping, gliding and sculling. By the end of this level children need to be able to skate the width of the rink with confidence using both feet along with demonstrating other building blocks. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 7: Rookie Patrol
description:
Rookie Patrol features timed 100-metre swims, 350-metre workouts and swimming while wearing clothes. A work-hard, play-hard approach develops swimming strength and efficiency with emphasis on 'Water Smart' behaviour. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 6. Swimmers continue developing front crawl, back crawl and breaststroke. Swimmers develop individual fitness to meet a timed 100m swim and 350m workout. Water proficiency skills include swimming with clothes, ready position, and feet-first/head-first surface dives. Demonstrating the ability to conduct a primary assessment and calling EMS are included as first aid skills. Victim recognition and throwing assists are other key elements of the program. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 8: Ranger Patrol
description:
Ranger Patrol features timed 200-metre swims, 100-metre fitness medley and the support of a 2.5 kg weight. Skill drills, including a non-contact rescue, enhance swimmers' capabilities in the water. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Prerequisite: Completed Swimmer 7 – Rookie Patrol. Ranger Patrol enhances capability in the water including stride entries and underwater, forward and backward somersaults. Swimmers learn lifesaving sport skills with a lifesaving stroke medley, timed object support and a non-contact rescue with a buoyant aid. Eggbeater kick and increased fitness levels are developed to meet a 200m timed swim. First aid focuses on unconscious victims and obstructed airway procedures. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Swimmer 9: Star Patrol
description:
Star Patrol features times 300-metre swims, 600-metre workouts, lifeguard whistle signals and airway and bleeding first aid priorities. This level demands good physical condition and lifesaving judgement. There is a non-refundable exam fee of $4.25.
Pre-requisite: Completed Swimmer 8 – Ranger Patrol. Star Patrol challenges swimmers with a 300m timed swim, 600m workout and a 25m object carry. Strokes are continued to be refined. Lifesaving skills include use of rescue aids, defense methods, victim removals and supporting a victim in shallow water. First aid focuses on treatment of bone or joint injuries and respiratory emergencies. Once complete, swimmers register into Bronze Star. A non-refundable exam/admin fee of $3.00 is applicable.
ageText: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs,

title: Reserve In Advance: Table Tennis All Ages
description:
Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. For all ages, children 6-12 years must be accompanied by a participating adult. Please arrive earl and check in at the front counter to claim your reservation. Participants arriving 10 minutes after activity start time will be considered an in person drop-in, subject to remaining availability.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Come Discover the Nordic Countries
description: Have you ever wondered what makes the Nordic countries so fascinating? Join us for a morning of discovery as we explore five remarkable destinations: Denmark, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, Norway, and Sweden.From charming Scandinavian cities and picturesque villages to dramatic fjords, breathtaking landscapes, and unique cultural traditions, we'll discover what makes each destination special and why these northern corners of the world capture the imagination of travellers.Whether these destinations are already on your travel wish list or you've never given them much thought, come with an open mind and curiosity in your heart. You may just discover somewhere that inspires your next adventure!Enjoy a morning of travel inspiration, interesting discoveries, and refreshments along the way.Come curious. Leave inspired!This workshop will be presented by Libby Adams. Libby operates Journeys By Libby.

title: Swim Instructor (for Adults)
description: ADULT PROGRAM. Participants please contact Alvin Cheung or Carson Croy before registering. The Swim Instructor is designed for those who wish to teach the Lifesaving Society's learn-to-swim programs. Candidates are trained using a competency-based model that walks them through teaching and evaluation philosophy and the techniques/approaches required to teach developing swimmers. Instructors also learn about long-term and short-term planning, class management, safety supervision, and the principles of evaluation. This course includes a supervised practice teaching component that will better prepare candidates for future job opportunities as an instructor. The Swim Instructor Kit is not included in the course fee and must be purchased at the front desk prior to the program start date. Prerequisite: Must be 15 years old by last day of the course and hold a Bronze Cross certificate (need not be current). Must have completed Adapted Swim Instructor Course - Online Session: Meeting the Needs of Diverse Swimmers found on the Lifesaving Society BC & Yukon branch website.

title: National Lifeguard Pool (for Adults)
description:
ADULT PROGRAM. Participants please contact Alvin Cheung or Carson Croy before registering. The NL Pool certification is designed to develop the fundamental values, judgment, knowledge, skills and fitness required by lifeguards. This course emphasizes the lifeguarding skills, principles and practices, and the decision-making processes that assist the lifeguard in providing effective safety supervision in swimming pool environments. Prerequisite: Bronze Cross (does not need to be current) and Standard First Aid or Aquatic Emergency Care (current award recommended) by the first day of the NL course. Emergency First Aid certificates obtained in high school are not accepted. Must be 15 years old by the last day of the course. Alert Manual is required and not included in fee. There is a non-refundable exam fee.
Students must be prepared to bring bathing suit, manual and paper for each class. Candidates will need to provide proof of the prerequisites on the 1st day of the course to the instructor or be sent home with no refund. Emergency First Aid certificates obtained in high school are not accepted. Recognized Agencies for Standard First Aid or Aquatic Emergency Care are: any Canadian branch of the Lifesaving Society, Canadian Red Cross, St John Ambulance, Canadian Heart and Stroke Foundation or Canadian Ski Patrol. 100% attendance is required.

title: Creating Professional Images of  Your Artwork - 2D Artwork
description:
Join professional photographer Kyla Bailey to learn skills and techniques that make a real difference in how your artwork is presented.
This workshop will cover:
  • Photographing paintings, drawings, prints, and other flat work.
  • Lighting techniques to avoid glare and reflections.
  • Achieving accurate colour and exposure.
  • Using a camera or smartphone effectively
  • Creating consistent, professional documentation for submissions, websites, portfolios, and grant applications.
  • Photo Editing techniques

About Kyla Bailey

Over the past 20 years I've worked as a professional photographer and lens-based artist, photographing artwork for museums, galleries, publications, and artists. During my time at both the Museum of Anthropology and the Vancouver Art Gallery, I photographed artwork for more than 25 published books, as well as documenting numerous exhibitions and installations. Those experiences gave me a deep understanding of how to create beautiful, professional images that faithfully represent an artist's work. Alongside my professional practice, I've also taught photography at Langara College and have always enjoyed helping others build confidence behind the camera.

title: Intro to Gliders
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Gliders skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. If you have basic skating experience please attend an evaluation session. In this level, children receive a facility tour, learn about safety on ice, how to fall down and stand up, and walk on ice without assistance, along with other building blocks to progress to the next level. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.
ageText: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 7 yrs,

title: Reserve In Advance:  Active Aging Yoga & Core
description:
Enjoy this energizing blend of yoga and core focused exercises, with the strength of other parts of the body will also be enhanced such as the back and legs. Breathing practice will also be introduced for balancing the energy level and nervous system. Suitable for both beginners and participants with yoga experience core exercises and yoga stretches for seniors. A Thera-band may be used. End the class with a beautiful relaxing savasana. Be strong from the inside out in this moderate level yoga/moving meditation class with core exercises.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.

title: Blades 1
description: This class is a prerequisite to the Blades skating program for the true beginner: those who have never been on the ice and those who do not know how to skate. In this level, children learn about safety on the ice, how to fall down and stand up, walk on the ice without assistance and are introduced to stopping, gliding and sculling. By the end of this level children need to be able to skate the width of the rink with confidence using both feet along with demonstrating other building blocks. A CSA approved hockey or snow sports helmet is mandatory for all skate lesson programs. If you require skate rentals, please purchase a skate rental pass on or before the first day of lessons. Please do not register your child for more than one lesson set at a time.

title: Piano: Private Lesson Long-Term Debbie Lin
description:
Students can sign up for private piano lessons from fall through spring. Instructor: TBA.
- Prorated Fees: Class fees will be adjusted based on the date of enrollment, beginning with the first scheduled class attended.- Private & Semi-Private Options: Select private lessons may be converted into semi-private sessions for two students upon request, please contact the Music and Media Arts Programmer for details. - Make-Up Lessons & Credits: Make-up classes or account credits are only issued in the event of instructor absence or an unexpected facility closure. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer make-up sessions or credits for student absences.
To give long-term arts students ample time to determine if a long-term program is right for them, students can attend 4 classes before a yearlong commitment is required. If you withdraw during this period, you will be charged only for each class you attend without being charged the City of Burnaby refund fee of 10%. Withdrawals/refunds are not permitted after the start of the 5th class of a long-term program. Payment plan option (via credit card payments) available: 50% of payment due at time of registration, 25% due on Dec 15, and 25% due on Mar 15.

title: Jr Golf | Play (age 8-10) | Skills Development | 8 weeks
description:
A 8-week program designed for developing golfers with some experience. You’ll level up your putting, short game, full swing, and decision-making through fun competitive drills and games, with the goal of playing at the pitch and putt.
Golfers will be provided an environment where they will be supported in development of skills. The achievement of standards leading to confident on course experience.
Level: Beg/int and Intermediate
Number of Classes: 8
Class Duration: 90 mins each
Min/Max number of participants:6
Students are expected to bring their own clubs for this program
Classes are conducted in rain or shine
Class cancellation / refund policy: 7 days' notice is required for cancellation and refund.

title: Reserve In Advance: Badminton All Ages
description:
Come play this drop-in indoor sport in a positive and enjoyable environment. Reserve in advance is available for this activity, check-in prior to activity start time to avoid losing your reservation.
Drop-ins are subject to remaining spots available. No waitlist.
Customers with a 10 Visit Be Active Pass will be required to pay the drop-in rate at the time of registration for a reserve in advance activity. On the day of your drop-in activity, please visit the front desk to have this charge refunded and a visit taken from your 10 Visit Be Active Pass. Customers with a valid Annual, One Month or Recurring Monthly Be Active Pass will be registered at no charge.
If you are unable to attend, please withdraw from the drop-in activity for the consideration to others. Withdraw online up until the day prior to the activity start date or contact a recreation facility prior to the start of the activity.
